pages.title: Overview
pages.description: A guide to chan: from your first terminal to remote devservers, gateways, and agent teams.

pages.title: Install & first run
pages.description: Install chan, make it your default terminal, file browser or Markdown editor on Linux, open the Computers screen, and turn a directory into a workspace.
pages.head: launcher-demo

pages.title: Terminal & teams
pages.description: Use terminal commands, rich prompts, drafts, program status, and agent teams.

pages.title: Navigation
pages.description: Arrange windows, panes, and tabs, and find actions with the command launcher.

pages.title: Command launcher
pages.description: Run any command, change a setting, or reach any window from one searchable list.

pages.title: tmux control mode
pages.description: Run tmux -CC in a chan terminal, locally or over ssh, and work with its windows and panes as Chan windows and panes.

pages.title: Editor & previews
pages.description: Edit text, preview Markdown, slide decks, and JSON, and export documents to PDF.

pages.title: File browser & reports
pages.description: Browse files, transfer them between machines, and inspect code reports and COCOMO estimates.

pages.title: Workspace search
pages.description: Find content, files, tags, and relationships through the search UI and terminal.

pages.title: Graph
pages.description: Navigate directories and relationships, and use depth to see more of a repository.

pages.title: Dashboard & index
pages.description: Read workspace information, follow indexing progress, and manage what gets indexed.

pages.title: Extensions
pages.description: Add your own applications as sandboxed tabs and integrate them through the host bridge and cs.

pages.title: Settings & defaults
pages.description: Configure appearance, editing, terminals, shortcuts, and workspace preferences.

pages.title: Screensavers
pages.description: Configure idle locking and explore the animations shown in an empty workspace.

pages.title: Devserver
pages.description: Set up a devserver and connect to its terminals and workspaces from the Computers window.

pages.title: systemd integration
pages.description: Run the devserver as a systemd user service, restart and upgrade it without losing terminals, and report its metrics to systemd-report.

pages.title: Chan in a browser
pages.description: Serve a workspace or a devserver from the chan binary alone and use it from any browser, no desktop needed.

pages.title: Collaboration & sessions
pages.description: Share workspace sessions, identify clients, and hand over leadership locally or remotely.

pages.title: Host a gateway
pages.description: Run your own gateway on one server and publish devservers behind sign-in, for you and the people you share them with.
